checks.title: Position ownership and liquidity interfaces observed
checks.detail: All successful reads refer to the recorded block. Interfaces can be imitated. Liquidity, NFT IDs and owed raw token quantities are different units; owed values are not a price or a guarantee of proceeds. Separate pool observations do not authenticate identity or a fair market price; signature acceptance, taxes and full exit economics remain unverified.

checks.title: Signature network and query provenance
checks.detail: The RPC network comes from the request or the claimed message domain. An independent provider snapshot is not bound to this signing origin or request; a match does not prove the signing network.

checks.title: Signature validity and future consumption remain unverified
checks.detail: Only an unsigned message is available. No signature was requested or generated, and no ecrecover, ERC-1271 isValidSignature, or Permit consumption was performed. Encoding and nonce/domain matches do not prove acceptance or safe future use.

checks.title: Declared DAI-style Permit authority identified
checks.detail: The supported DAI schema signs holder, spender, nonce, submission expiry and allowed. Under the reference implementation allowed=true maps to the maximum uint256 allowance; false maps to zero. The mapped amount is derived semantics, not a separately signed value. A matching type graph does not prove DAI identity; some same-shaped tokens have different expiry semantics.

checks.title: Signing account code observed
checks.detail: No account code was observed at this block. This does not prove private-key control or exclude an undeployed smart account or future delegation.

checks.title: Verifier code observation
checks.detail: Code is observed only on the stated network and block. Code presence does not establish protocol identity, standard behavior, or safety.

checks.title: Typed-message domain separator comparison
checks.detail: The message domain hash matches the contract return value. This does not establish contract trust or actual signature validity.

checks.title: Declared asset owner compared with signing account
checks.detail: This compares the committed owner, DAI holder or ERC-3009 payer with the signing account. It is not cryptographic signature verification. A difference requires review of the authority and any contract-account extension.

checks.title: Signature submission deadline compared with block time
checks.detail: Under the DAI reference implementation expiry=0 has no submission deadline; a nonzero expiry allows submission through that timestamp. It does not limit allowance duration after submission. Same-shaped implementations may differ and are not authenticated.

checks.detail: The supported ERC-3009 schema commits to payer, recipient, exact amount and an open validity window. It does not set an ERC-20 allowance. ReceiveWithAuthorization requires the future caller to be the recipient under the standard; neither future caller nor actual consumption is observed. Implementation identity and signature acceptance remain unverified.
